ops.statement: A lesson pasted into a delegated agent's own launch order is NOT thereby applied. commander-301 was handed lesson:prove-command-fails-postcondition verbatim in LAUNCH_ORDER-301 'Active lessons relevant to this mission', and still authored three 'the writer REJECTS X' postconditions as check:null attestations rather than as ! <command> bash-negation checks. The miss was caught only by a cold plan critic with no authoring context. Treat an inherited-lessons list as a checklist to be VERIFIED against the authored artifact by a fresh reader, not as context that conditions the author.

ops.statement: When converging a design-it-twice panel, the convergence author is prone to over-claiming unanimity across candidates - reporting as 'the panel settled this' what only a majority held. commander-301's first comparison claimed six unanimous decisions; a cold critic found two were false and a third overstated, verified mechanically (durable_root appeared in candidates A:1 B:5 C:0 D:0, while the comparison claimed all four, and the recommended candidate was one of the silent two). Manufactured consensus is worse than a plain recommendation because it presents the author's preference as the panel's verdict, removing it from the human's decision. Verify every cross-candidate claim with a command before floating a comparison.
